title: OpenAI and AMD Show How AI Can Accelerate Chip Design
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

OpenAI says its models helped improve the power, performance and area (PPA) of circuitry in AMD’s flagship GPU by up to 14% against baselines that engineers had already heavily optimized. OpenAI describes the work as roughly a year’s worth of engineering progress in under five months. Some of those improvements made it into a design recently released for manufacturing, according to OpenAI President and co-founder Greg Brockman. AMD added other changes to its production design files for future versions.

The models rewrote SystemVerilog code that governs how circuits perform calculations, handle control operations and move data. Synopsys design tools checked that the rewritten circuits behaved as intended and measured the trade-offs among power, speed and area. AMD also verified single-digit percentage PPA gains in key blocks of its upcoming flagship CPU using model-written designs. Together, the GPU and CPU results suggest that AI-assisted optimization can help across several kinds of circuitry.

OpenAI reported another encouraging result from Jalapeño, its first custom inference chip, developed with Broadcom. The company said it validated the chip in physical silicon and estimates that model-proposed changes reduced the standard-cell area of its matrix unit by about 10%. AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su welcomed the results on X, writing that she was proud of the work.

The opportunity is to give chip designers more chances to test promising ideas within a fixed schedule. A circuit improvement that once demanded weeks of manual iteration could become practical to explore alongside several alternatives. Engineers can then use the same verification tools they already trust to decide which changes belong in a production design. The fact that some of AMD’s improvements reached tape-out shows how that workflow can carry an idea from a model-generated rewrite all the way to a design ready for manufacturing. That’s a meaningful step for AI-assisted engineering.

OpenAI’s technical report, Nov. 18 — The primary source for the reported PPA gains of up to 14% in AMD’s flagship GPU circuitry, the single-digit CPU gains, the Synopsys verification process, and the estimated 10% area reduction in Jalapeño’s matrix unit.
